## Outcome and change brief

G-01a/G-01b configured native selector-adapter prerequisite; POAM-009 and OBJ-12 remain open. Public main `291fee511887932572ecc9935e9786e098727677`, with PR198 `63375dd42c77986ea8bd64a9c6034c07af2d3c9a` integrated by ordinary merge. Opening head `c9de56cd47337f2d87fc1812392873208144a50d`. Land #196 and #198 first. Draft brief precedes implementation.

Current behavior: actual BF16 output has only been captured by an offline Python experiment and decoded by the pure Rust contract. No native configured chat transport exists for the engine to compose. Target: an optional stateless Rust adapter in `rrd-inference` that sends one explicitly prepared bounded request to a configured binding, validates the actual response with the choice contract and returns bounded observations. It grants no authority, installs no engine handler and never dispatches the chosen worker.

Exact scope: `rrd-inference/src/endpoint_chat.rs`, its `lib.rs` export and optional Cargo feature/dependency/lock entries; focused tests based on retained actual endpoint records and explicit denial mutations; an operator example for actual transport verification; the owning inference reference, one Gate G journal and generated navigation/inventory. No fixed model/provider ranking, endpoint, task keyword, prompt template or credential source in library behavior. Typed protocol fields and resource ceilings are validation rules. Existing embedding registry, budgets, model-load handshake and three routing decisions remain unchanged.

Engine construction of context/candidates, authenticated task/source admission, durable attempt reservation/fencing and public operation registration remain missing. The adapter consumes prepared values and caller-owned execution bounds; it is not a competing lifecycle. A failed or cancelled dispatched call remains potentially executed; no retries, redirect following, implicit environment proxy, background replacement worker or claimed provider hard-stop. Credentials are resolved through an explicit caller-supplied reference resolver and never serialized/logged. TLS is required outside literal loopback. Strong loaded-weight identity and hard termination are unavailable until separately qualified.

## Inspection, oracle and acceptance

Inspected engine inference and durable reasoning-budget reservation/completion, inference registry/control, endpoint configuration/binding/selection contracts, Gate G/I, dependency readiness and transport architecture constraints. Reuse configuration identities and the existing cancellation/deadline mechanism. No engine budget or provider-specific state is created.

First oracle: the configured actual BF16 endpoint cannot be called through a native selector adapter. Retain actual request/response bytes and digests for the real maintenance task, plus failure/timeout observations; no fabricated provider output or training labels. Denial probes derive from retained real records and never enter training. Test stale/foreign configuration, model mismatch, network denial, deadline/cancellation before dispatch, secret-free failures, bounded output, truncation and invalid choices.

Run focused adapter tests, owning package tests, strict Clippy/format, documentation/navigation/workflow/inventory checks, then required full candidate CI. Optional-feature CI already exercises all `rrd-inference` features. Native live calls prove transport compatibility only; no benchmark or model quality claim.

Research: inspect pinned ureq configuration/body/timeout docs and source, plus vLLM's official chat-compatible transport reference. Use an optional locked HTTP/TLS client rather than handwritten HTTP/TLS. Trace raw request/response identity and elapsed time as observations; no invented usage/cost. Stop for architecture expansion, unverifiable actual output, secret leakage, unbounded response handling, embedded routing preference or required-check bypass. All integration and completion claims wait for their actual engine acceptance evidence.
title: Add bounded native controller chat transport
